title: 15-second urban parkour prompt template
prompt_text:
15-Second Urban Parkour Prompt Template | Safe Wall-Vault Version". Model: Kling 4.0 (on PixVerse). Date: 4:30 PM · Oct 30, 2026. Likes 1 · Reposts 0 · Views 375.
  Full prompt (exact, as written — very long multi-section production prompt):
  "15-Second Urban Parkour Prompt Template | Safe Wall-Vault Version】A 15-second live-action cinematic urban parkour short film, 16:9, 24 fps, realistic 4K film quality. Blue hour after rainfall, set inside an enclosed rooftop mechanical courtyard on a modern city high-rise. Wet concrete surfaces, mechanical rooms, ventilation pipes, maintenance stairs, sloped ramps, billboard support frames, multilevel service platforms, and an internal rooftop partition wall form a three-dimensional parkour route. The entire rooftop is one continuous, solid architectural structure surrounded by a sturdy two-meter-high protective perimeter wall. Every parkour action takes place in the central rooftop area, at least three meters away from the exterior edge. There are no gaps between buildings, no rooftop-to-rooftop jumps, no movement near exposed edges, and no jumping toward the street below. The distant skyline and city lights appear only as background scenery above the protective walls, creating urban scale without placing a visible abyss beneath the character. 【Core Contrast】The protagonist appears to be a very small blonde girl in bright clothing, yet she runs with extraordinary speed, calm judgment, exceptional coordination, explosive power, and route awareness far beyond what her appearance suggests. The contrast must be expressed through observable behavior: her short legs generate an exceptionally fast and precise cadence; her small hands identify support points before her body reaches each obstacle; her eyes always locate the next landing point before her head moves; transitions between movements contain almost no hesitation. She is not a magical character or a superhero. Every action obeys realistic gravity, body weight, joint movement, physical contact, momentum, and impact. 【Character Lock】The protagonist appears approximately five years old: a blonde girl of European descent with realistic young-child height and body proportions, a round youthful face, pale golden slightly curly hair tied into two loose pigtails, and thin red round-frame glasses. Her transparent lenses reveal clear blue-gray eyes with natural blinking, subtle eye movements, moisture, and living catchlights. She wears a bright yellow lightweight windbreaker, turquoise athletic shorts, rainbow-striped leggings, purple-red running shoes, and a small orange sports backpack. Her vivid children's clothing strongly contrasts with the cool gray urban rooftop. Her round glasses, pigtails, clothing colors, and backpack position remain completely consistent throughout every third-person shot. The glasses may slide slightly down her nose after a hard landing; she quickly pushes them back into place with a small nose scrunch, never slowing down, looking at the camera, or striking a heroic pose. Objective: cross the mechanical courtyard, vault over the central partition wall, and strike the red finish button before the rooftop timer turns red. 【Safe Spatial Layout】The route contains several internal rooftop elevations: The starting point is a maintenance platform approximately 0.8 meters above the main rooftop, connected to it by four wide stairs. A ventilation pipe approximately 0.6 meters high stands in the center of the main rooftop. Beside the rooftop mechanical room is a service platform approximately 0.9 meters above the main roof. A wide sloped ramp behind the platform returns to the main rooftop level. The primary obstacle is a 1.1-meter-high internal concrete partition wall located in the middle of the rooftop. Behind the partition wall is a continuous rooftop landing area approximately five meters wide and more than eight meters deep. The finish button is installed on the exterior wall of a mechanical room inside the rooftop courtyard. The partition wall is only an internal functional divider. It is not an exterior building wall, parapet, perimeter wall, or rooftop edge. Continuous concrete rooftop flooring must always be visible on both sides of the wall. 【Camera Rules】Use six clearly paced shots, alternating between a close rear-following shot, first-person POV, third-person side view, front-following shot, and low-angle tracking shot. Use 17–24mm wide-angle lenses with approximately 4%–6% subtle barrel distortion, slight perspective stretching, and natural lens breathing near the edges. Keep the subject near the central image area so her face, glasses, and limbs remain undistorted. Fast movement includes restrained camera shake, realistic motion blur, and subtle rolling-shutter behavior. Cuts occur on foot impacts, hand contacts, structural occlusions, or fast whip-pans. 【Absolute First-Person POV Rules】Every first-person shot must present a clean, unobstructed, authentic POV. The image must never show the round glasses, eyeglass rims, lens reflections, eyeglass shadows, nose bridge, cheeks, eyelashes, hair, or any part of the girl's face. First-person shots may show only her hands, forearms, and occasionally her knees or shoe tips. The image must not look as if it is being viewed through glasses, and no glasses-shaped border may appear around the frame. When the video cuts back to third person, the round glasses must still be correctly positioned on her face, preserving character continuity. 【Shot One | 0–2 Seconds | Close Rear Follow】A 17mm low-angle tracking shot follows at the girl's waist height. She is already sprinting across a maintenance platform approximately 0.8 meters above the main rooftop. Her small legs generate an extremely rapid cadence as her bright yellow jacket, blonde pigtails, and orange backpack whip with the movement. The camera remains slightly behind and to one side. City lights form a distant skyline above the high perimeter protection wall. Four wide concrete stairs connect the platform to the main rooftop. She does not jump from the platform edge. Instead, she runs rapidly down the staircase: her first stride covers two steps, her second lands on the next step, and her final stride enters the continuous main rooftop. Her shoes make clear contact with each step, and her body lowers progressively with the staircase. The camera descends with her. Each footfall produces a short visual impact, and she accelerates immediately after reaching the main rooftop without pausing. The music begins with a delicate music-box motif. Her four stair impacts synchronize with four progressively stronger electronic percussion hits. 【Shot Two | 2–4 Seconds | First-Person POV】Cut to a clean first-person POV at the authentic eye level of a small child. The image has only restrained vertical movement produced by running. Do not show glasses, eyeglass frames, lens edges, the nose bridge, eyelashes, cheeks, hair, or any facial feature. A ventilation pipe approximately 0.6 meters high stands ahead. Continuous rooftop flooring is clearly visible beyond it. Two small hands enter from the bottom of the frame and press accurately against the top of the pipe. Her body uses its forward momentum to perform a compact straddle vault. Her gaze targets the hand-contact point first, then immediately moves toward the safe landing area beyond the pipe. Her shoes and knees may briefly enter the bottom of the frame as both feet land on the same rooftop level. A sharp industrial percussion hit accompanies her hands contacting the metal. A brief whoosh follows her body over the pipe. The complete breakbeat enters when her feet strike the rooftop. 【Shot Three | 4–6.3 Seconds | Third-Person Lateral Rise】A 24mm third-person side-tracking shot. The girl sprints toward the exterior wall of a rooftop mechanical room. A fixed equipment base approximately 0.4 meters high stands beside the wall, leading to a service platform approximately 0.9 meters above the main rooftop. Her left foot lands on the equipment base, and her right foot immediately plants against the mechanical-room wall. She performs a diagonal upward tic-tac. Both hands accurately catch the edge of the service platform, her right knee reaches the surface first, and her body rapidly moves onto the platform. The upward force comes primarily from her legs. Her hands guide the movement rather than pulling her upward. She does not hang, pause, or rise without physical support. The camera rises approximately 0.9 meters with her and tilts upward slightly. The equipment base, wall-contact point, and upper landing surface remain visible at the same time. After she reaches the platform, her glasses slide slightly down her nose; one quick nose scrunch pushes them back into position. Stepping onto the base, planting against the wall, and entering the platform correspond to three progressively stronger industrial beats. 【Shot Four | 6.3–8.3 Seconds | Front Follow Into Low Slide】An 18mm low frontal tracking shot moves backward as the girl sprints toward the camera across the service platform. A wide sloped ramp ahead reconnects the platform to the lower main rooftop. She runs down the ramp instead of jumping from the platform edge. The camera lowers with her, keeping her face and complete body readable. At the bottom of the ramp, a billboard support frame crosses the route. Her eyes identify the opening beneath the structure, her shoulders drop, and her body changes from an upright sprint into a low sliding posture. One hand briefly brushes the wet concrete to control direction. Her shoes create believable friction against the surface, and water droplets pass the edge of the lens. The camera moves backward close to the ground while the support columns create rapid foreground occlusions. The music reduces its low frequencies as she enters the ramp. The bass slams back into the track as she slides beneath the support frame. 【Shot Five | 8.3–11.6 Seconds | Main Third-Person Wall Vault】This is the central action of the sequence: vaulting over an internal rooftop partition wall. She is not vaulting over an exterior building wall, crossing between buildings, or jumping from the rooftop. A 24mm third-person front-side wide shot simultaneously shows the complete partition wall, the approach area, the girl's full body, and the wide rooftop landing area behind the wall. The wall is approximately 1.1 meters high and 0.3 meters thick. The flooring on both sides is at exactly the same elevation. The composition must clearly prove that both sides of the partition wall contain continuous, solid rooftop flooring. There is no cliff, building gap, staircase, or vertical drop behind the wall. The girl receives approximately four meters of running distance. Her small legs accelerate with an exceptionally fast cadence while her eyes lock onto the top of the wall and the landing point behind it. On the final step, she drives against the ground and places both hands on the top of the wall. Her shoulders move beyond the support point, her knees tuck tightly toward her chest, and both legs sweep compactly around the side of her body in a professional speed vault. The camera tracks rapidly parallel to the wall. As her body clears the top, it rises approximately 0.5 meters so that the landing area behind the wall remains continuously visible. She follows a short, low trajectory and lands approximately one meter beyond the wall. Her knees and hips compress on impact while her body retains forward momentum. She does not fall downward. She immediately takes two additional steps and accelerates again. The kick drum drops out briefly before takeoff, leaving only the music-box motif and her breathing. Her hands contacting the wall trigger a metallic accent. The first frame of both feet landing triggers the strongest musical drop in the entire sequence. 【Shot Six | 11.6–15 Seconds | Low Third-Person Into Close Follow】A 16mm low-angle camera is positioned behind the partition wall, facing the landing zone. The girl's feet enter the frame and strike the rooftop. Her knees and hips compress, and her body continues into a rapid shoulder roll. The camera immediately circles to her rear-side position and becomes a close tracking shot. Two rows of enormous ventilation units lead toward a red finish button mounted on the mechanical-room wall. She uses extremely short steps to change direction rapidly between the machines, alternating left and right foot placement while keeping her body close to the equipment. Her tiny, brightly colored figure strongly contrasts with the enormous industrial structures. For the final three meters, she accelerates at full speed, her eyes locking onto the red button before her head turns. Her right hand strikes the button just before the timer changes to red. The button produces a sharp bell sound. She does not celebrate. She braces her hands against her knees and breathes rapidly. Her round glasses slide down after the final impact; she pushes them back up with one finger and looks toward the stopped timer. Cut immediately to black. 【Character Performance】Her speed must come from extremely high cadence, short ground-contact time, rapid weight transfer, and seamless action transitions—not rigid acceleration, time-lapse movement, or footage played at increased speed. Her eyes move before her head, continuously scanning grip points, the top of the wall, landing surfaces, and exits. In third-person shots, natural micro-saccades, realistic blinking, moisture, and living catchlights remain visible through her glasses. Her tactics change for each obstacle: She uses rapid foot placement on the stairs and never jumps from the platform. She uses hand support to vault the ventilation pipe. She uses the equipment base and wall for a tic-tac ascent. She uses the connected ramp to descend. She lowers her posture to slide beneath the billboard frame. She uses a speed vault to cross the internal partition wall. She uses a shoulder roll to dissipate landing impact. She does not display emotions for the camera, smile toward the viewer, stop, or pose. Her concentration is expressed through continuously locating the next landing point and immediately solving each physical obstacle. 【Background Music】Original 160 BPM industrial breakbeat and drum-and-bass score built around the contrast of a bright music-box melody and heavy urban low frequencies. The delicate celesta motif represents the girl's small, colorful appearance. Tight kick drums, short snares, rapid chopped breaks, metallic industrial percussion, gritty Reese bass, and deep sub-bass express her extraordinary speed. Rhythmic synchronization: 0–2 seconds: music-box opening; four stair contacts synchronize with four progressively stronger beats. 2–4 seconds: the complete drum pattern enters during the ventilation-pipe vault. 4–6.3 seconds: stepping onto the base, planting against the wall, and entering the platform correspond to three ascending accents. 6.3–8.3 seconds: low frequencies reduce during the ramp descent; the bass returns as she slides beneath the structure. 8.3–11.6 seconds: percussion density increases during the wall-vault approach; the beat briefly drops out before takeoff; successful landing triggers the strongest musical drop. 11.6–15 seconds: the full high-speed rhythm continues. Her final three steps correspond to three escalating beats. The button bell, a short bass stab, and the cut to black occur simultaneously. The action sounds must remain audible through the music. Briefly duck the score during foot impacts, hand contacts, wall plants, slides, wall-vault landings, and the button bell. No lyrics, vocals, or rap. 【Realistic Film Quality】Live-action cinematic realism with authentic child skin texture, fine facial hair, naturally flushed cheeks, moist eyes, and physically accurate reflections in the lenses. Realistic strands of blonde hair, fabric folds, shoe compression, splashing water, wet concrete, rusted metal, and condensation. Blue-hour ambient light contrasts with warm city illumination. Subtle film grain, natural depth of field, and realistic motion blur. No excessive sharpening, plastic skin, or video-game rendering. 【Strict Prohibitions】No rooftop-to-rooftop jumps, jumping from the building, jumping from an exterior rooftop edge, jumping toward the street, free fall, crossing gaps between buildings, hanging from a rooftop edge, missteps, falling, or a camera falling from the roof. Do not transform the internal partition wall into an exterior building wall, parapet, perimeter wall, or cliff edge. Continuous, wide, same-level rooftop flooring must remain visible on both sides of the partition wall. First-person footage must never show glasses, eyeglass frames, lens edges, lens reflections, the nose bridge, cheeks, eyelashes, hair, or any facial outline. The first-person image must never resemble a view through glasses. No flying, weightless floating, double jumps, midair direction changes, superhero movements, impactless landings, foot sliding, action resets, or character teleportation. Do not transform the girl into a teenager or adult. No adult body proportions, mature facial features, adult makeup, or adult-styled clothing. No disappearing or deformed glasses, hairstyle changes, clothing-color changes, backpack position changes, additional limbs, malformed fingers, reversed joints, bodies passing through equipment, heavy fisheye distortion, stretched facial features, melting architecture, slow motion, dialogue, subtitles, text, watermarks, or brand logos.

title: Stickman survival-thriller animation skill built in code
prompt_text: <inputs> Ask me for: my video idea (one line is fine), the setting, the length (60-90 s) and the narrator (an ElevenLabs voice, or "free" for a local text-to-speech). Everything is built in code: no AI images, no AI video. Make it MY story, not a copy of an example. </inputs> <format> The style is a second-person survival thriller with stickmen, built as a series: - "Imagine you…" hook with a time stamp in the first 3 s - a HUD with the DAY number and a clock that moves forward through the episode - 3-4 RULES, each one paid off on screen - a threat that escalates and is mostly shown, not told - a twist that makes one rule impossible - a two-choice ending ("DO YOU OPEN IT?" style, a green and a red option, "COMMENT BELOW") and "FOLLOW FOR DAY 2" Around 20-30 voice lines, 60-90 s, a new shot every 1.5-3 s. </format> <story> Write a beat sheet and the script first and show me both before building anything. - One line = one visual. Rules are short commands. - Open a new question every ~10 s and only answer it with a bigger one. - Put the viewer in POV for the scary parts: what you see through a door, a window, a phone, a peephole. - The ending is a choice where both options look bad. - Write numbers twice: the caption form ("11:58 PM") and the spoken form ("eleven fifty-eight P M") for the text-to-speech. - Rotate settings between episodes (apartment, subway, school at night, hospital, cabin, plane, office, motel) and fit the threat to the setting. </story> <look> Pick a palette per story, but keep the language: - real 3D low-poly sets with real lights and shadows; the mood comes from light (one warm practical, one cold fill, one strong accent such as a door gap, a screen or a siren) - the stickman is flat and 2D-looking: a light body with a thick dark outline, round strokes, dot eyes, no mouth; give the main character one mark (a scar, a cap, a colour) so doubles and callbacks read - the overlay: a monospace HUD top-left, chunky captions (1-3 words, key words in an accent colour), a tilted rule sticker with a big condensed title, phone screens drawn in 2D - banned: AI frames, glossy 3D characters, emojis, music with vocals, long captions </look> <shots> A library to adapt to the story (never use all of them): - the opener: a camera move that starts tight on you and pulls out to show where you are - POV phone in your hands (2D phone UI, two stick thumbs) - a macro on the one detail that matters - outside chaos from above (balcony, bridge, window): physics vehicles, a running crowd, something collapsing or burning - third-person action in the room: walking with planted feet, reaching, hesitating, barricading - POV interaction: throwing, holding a torch, opening something - a close-up of your face for the reaction - a low angle on a door or vent: light leaking in, shadows moving - knocks, shakes, things falling - a fisheye peephole, camera or window view of the threat stepping closer - the choice screen and the end card </shots> <tools> What each tool is for. Install whatever is missing, and ask me before anything paid: - three.js: the 3D engine; it runs inside a web page. Download its module file locally so renders don't depend on the internet. Use its post-processing passes for bloom, plus one custom lens shader for vignette, grain, fisheye and colour fringing. - cannon-es: a JavaScript physics engine for vehicles, falling debris and collapses. - Playwright (Python): opens the page in a real browser (Edge or Chrome with the GPU on) and captures every frame as an image. - ffmpeg: the command-line video and audio tool. It joins the frames into an MP4, cuts and filters the audio (highpass, lowpass and echo for voices behind doors), mixes, normalises loudness and makes the phone-size copy. - ElevenLabs, or Kokoro (free local text-to-speech), for the narrator. - faster-whisper: free local speech-to-text with word timestamps. Use it to cut the voice cleanly and to time every caption. - numpy and Pillow: to check audio levels and make contact sheets of stills. - Sound: free downloaded sound effects from Mixkit (never synthesized) and a dark cinematic drone or tension bed with no vocals. </tools> <build> 1. One HTML page (film.html) with the 3D renderer at 1080x1920 drawn into a 2D canvas that also holds the overlay. A function window.seek(t) draws frame t and must be a pure function of time; every cut, sound and move is keyed to the word times. 2. Stickman. Draw each figure with 2D canvas strokes onto its own texture and put it on a plane that always faces the camera, with an alpha test so it casts a real shadow and slight emissive so it reads in the dark. Pose with joint angles, and walk with 2-bone IK so the planted foot never slides. 3. Physics and cloth. Simulate once at load with a fixed timestep, record the positions, then sample them by time, so every render is identical. Cloth (sheets, curtains, flags) is a verlet particle grid with wall and floor collisions and pinned points you can release. 4. Voice. If you generate one long take, never cut it at the API's character timestamps: they drift and slice words. Transcribe the take with faster-whisper word timestamps, match it to the script, cut only in real silence between lines, and only add pause where the natural one is too short. 5. Captions. Re-transcribe each final line, normalise numbers ("6:42" = "6 42", "AM" = "a m"), align the caption words to what was heard, and snap each word to its real start in the audio. Check that every caption has voice under it within ~120 ms. 6. Render. Playwright steps window.seek through every frame at 30 fps, and ffmpeg encodes a high-quality master, then a phone copy under 30 MB. 7. Mix with ffmpeg: the voice on top, the music about 12-14 dB under it, one sound effect per event, a dip before the big moment, loudness at -14 LUFS, then a scan for dropouts. </build> <gotchas> - fov is narrow: a normal lens sees very little sideways, so use wider lenses indoors and keep the subject close to the aim point. - Glass behind a solid frame is invisible: build mirrors and windows as a frame around a real hole. - Dust spread everywhere reads as stars, so keep it inside light beams. - Night shots go black after compression, so give each one a cold fill light. - Fog swallows distant things. - Never judge a reference or your own render from one frame every few seconds; check motion at the full frame rate. - Check cuts, captions and audio joints with numbers before every full render. </gotchas> <start> Ask me for the idea, show me the beat sheet and script, then 6 stills of the key shots before rendering the full video. </start>
